Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: premium personal research portfolio spotlight thumbnail, near-square 1.05:1 composition, 1536 x 1464 or closest supported size.
Primary request: a striking sculptural editorial cover for an independent replication study of PRH-JEPA, exploring how separately trained vision and text encoders can learn equivalent geometry up to rotation. It must communicate representation alignment at thumbnail scale.
Scene/backdrop: warm ivory archival drafting paper and a seamless sand-coloured tabletop. A restrained technical drawing grid with a few extremely fine graphite construction arcs and precise registration marks, spacious, no interface.
Subject: one beautifully crafted scientific alignment instrument, presented as a museum-quality 3D still life. Two large thin square transparent smoked-glass coordinate plates, suspended side-by-side above low travertine plinths. Each plate holds the SAME sparse asymmetric constellation of 9 substantial spherical nodes and slender connecting rods: left constellation burnished copper-orange; right constellation dark oxidised teal. The right constellation is the identical geometry rigidly rotated about 35 degrees in its plane, clearly recognizable as the same shape. Small ivory landscape bas-relief tile at the foot of the left plate, small ivory text-line bas-relief tile at the foot of the right plate. These tiles are symbols only. A single elegant partial graphite circular calibration arc between the plates hints at the rotation; no shared training network, no merged encoder. The two plates and geometries are the whole focal point, imposing and tactile.
Style/medium: sophisticated architectural model photography meets an art-directed scientific editorial illustration; physically plausible stone, dark charcoal metal, etched glass, fine paper grain. Crisp intentional shapes, premium craftsmanship, no generic AI cyber imagery.
Composition/framing: three-quarter isometric view, slightly elevated camera, tightly composed strong central silhouette occupying 75% of image, clean margins for a rounded crop. Large constellation nodes legible in a small card. Balanced orange and teal. No disconnected little decorative objects.
Lighting/mood: soft afternoon studio light from upper left, beautiful contact shadows, controlled contrast, quiet intellectual confidence.
Color palette: warm sand and ivory 70%, deep charcoal 20%, copper orange and oxidised teal 10%. Restrained rich accent colours.
Text: none. No lettering, words, title, numbers, labels, logos, watermark, charts, badges or pseudo code.
Constraints: this is conceptual artwork, not measured experimental evidence. Show equivalent geometry under one rigid rotation only, no growth, no improvement curve, no prediction of universal convergence. Two independent representations, not a joint image-text model. Full bleed, professional final artwork.

Primary request: an editorial visual metaphor for the two view-construction strategies tested in the independent PRH-JEPA study. Two balanced sculptural arrangements on the same tabletop, separated by generous clear space.
LEFT arrangement: one small square ivory bas-relief scene depicting a simple sailboat on water with a sun above. Above and behind it are THREE separate translucent ivory caption-like cards fanned gently apart; each has a different arrangement of raised horizontal teal line segments indicating different human descriptions of the same scene. No actual letters. Fine separate teal threads connect each distinct card down toward the shared scene tile; no encoder or convergence output.
RIGHT arrangement: one long ivory caption-like card with copper raised horizontal segments. In front of it are THREE overlapping shorter physical cut-paper strips visibly cut from that one card, repeated arrangements and some square charcoal masks occluding the segments. Delicate copper threads connect each crop back to the single original caption card. No scissors, no literal damage.
Composition: two equal visual groups with equal lighting, scale and space, arranged left and right on two simple low plinths. Left is multiple distinct scene descriptions; right is masked overlapping crops from a single description. Make the relationship exceptionally readable as a tactile physical arrangement. No arrows implying superiority, no check marks, crosses, winners, trophies, improved scores or common representation destinations. This image explains experimental inputs only, it does not claim an isolated causal or universal outcome. Warm paper backdrop, restrained fine drafting registration marks.

Primary request: an elegant sculptural visual metaphor for investigating how coordinate clipping changes a representation-alignment measurement under rotation.
Subject: a tabletop scientific specimen presented in THREE orderly stations from left to right, visually clear and restrained. First station: an upright thin smoked-glass square coordinate frame with a sparse copper-orange asymmetric constellation of 8 substantial nodes and slender rods inside it; include one node near the top right boundary. Second station: an identical frame containing the same copper-orange constellation rotated rigidly in its own plane, accompanied by a delicate partial circular graphite calibration arc. Third station: another identical frame at the same orientation as station two, with a clearly visible matte charcoal square aperture/grid mask at the edges. The copper structure is visible through this fixed coordinate boundary, with its outermost point visibly pressed inward at the boundary and a few short muted teal trace lines recording changed geometry. A thin horizontal ivory threshold rail lies across the third frame near the top, suggesting a coordinate cutoff. No points flying away and no smashed glass.
Composition: three equal glass specimens on low ivory travertine bases, long gallery-like arrangement, slightly elevated three-quarter view, lots of clean space around them. Keep their geometric forms sparse and legible, not a dense scientific chart. Subtle graphite drafting lines show the fixed coordinate axes in all three frames, not changing with the specimen. The story is geometry, rotation, then an axis-based clipping intervention; it must not look like a successful filtering pipeline or a model getting smarter.
Constraints: no axis labels, numbers, data values, drawn plots or claims about experimental scores. Artwork is only a conceptual accompaniment to the real measured figures. Equal visual prominence and neutral lighting at all stations.
